Pitchfork: The 200 Best Albums of the 1960s

podcast.body: Released in 1969, this album by The Shaggs is considered one of the great cult records of the last 50 years. It is described as "weird" and "hard to listen to," often guaranteed to clear a party. Despite its unusual qualities, Kurt Cobain ranked it as number five on his top 50 albums of all time. "The result was a record called Philosophy of the World... That is one of the great cult records from the last 50 years. It is weird, it is hard to listen to, and guaranteed to chase everybody out of a party at the end of the night."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The album was reissued by RCA Records in 1999 and has remained in print ever since, attesting to its enduring cult following. Its initial reception for being "so bad" paradoxically made it legendary, leading to its re-evaluation and widespread availability. "The cult of the shags is now so big that RCA records reissued Philosophy of the World in 1999, and have kept it in print ever since."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was recorded in less than a day, featuring 12 songs by the trio of sisters from New Hampshire. Despite being considered "not that good" by conventional standards, it earned legendary status and was praised for the sincerity and authenticity of its heartfelt performances. "The shags with the title track of their 1969 album Philosophy of the World, and yes I know it's not that good."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
